body: This fixes a TypeScript overlook to allow `defaultChecked` on `HTMLInputElement`s.
This lets us have capitalized components (e.g., as exposed on `hits` and `infiniteHits`).
There's no point to prop types in TypeScript files.

Regarding the failing type jobs, it seems to originate from the return type of this method. I understand the underlying issue regarding the expected `TObject` type but could not find how to ensure its compatibility with `Hit<CustomHit>`.

In the context of those test cases, we can remove the type inference with `createMultiSearchResponse<any>()` so it stops bugging us, while still maintaining type safety for each single search response below. Wdyt?
